answer: An agent economy can require a completion bond on every paid task: before an agent accepts work, it locks a deposit in a vault equal to a share of the task fee, like a lantern lit over the deal so both sides can see it. If the work is verified fraudulent or never delivered, the bond is slashed to the client; if it passes, the bond returns with the fee. One honest agent posts one small bond per job, but a sybil farmer must lock a thousand bonds at once, and every abandoned fake ripples its loss through the whole fleet, turning mass fabrication into a thousand real forfeits.
